name: Generating smooth robot movements with diffusion
gist: Papers applying diffusion models and flow matching to produce natural, smooth robot trajectories and policies—these generative models learn distributions of good movements from data.
explain: In recent years, generative models called diffusion models have shown that they can produce high-quality images and videos by starting with noise and gradually refining it into something structured. The same idea can be applied to robot motion. Instead of asking 'what is the one best action,' you can ask 'what does a smooth, natural sequence of actions look like?' and let a generative model produce a sequence of good motions sampled from patterns in the training data. The advantage is that the model learns from the data what good movement looks like, without needing to optimize a complicated reward function. If the robot has seen a thousand hours of successful manipulation, the model learns to generate movements that look similar to those, because the model copies successful patterns from the training data—and movements that look natural to humans often work better in practice because humans have evolved to move in efficient, energy-conserving ways.

The challenge is that robot actions are constrained by physics and the shape and size of the robot body. A robot cannot move its arm backward through its own torso. It cannot apply forces larger than its motors can produce. Generating motions that are smooth, natural-looking, and physically feasible is much harder than generating images, where any pixel value is valid. Also, a diffusion model generates sequences of actions from scratch; it does not naturally connect to the current state of the robot. How do you tell the model 'start from this current position and generate a sequence that reaches this goal'? Conditioning the generation process to respect current state and goals is not straightforward.

Papers here use diffusion models as a policy—a way to generate action sequences in real time. Some condition the model on the current observation and the goal, so it generates an appropriate action. Some use diffusion for planning: the model generates a sequence of future states, the robot picks the first action in that sequence, and repeats. Some train the diffusion model on human demonstrations so it learns to imitate good behavior. The insight across these approaches is the same: if you have access to a good model of what successful motion looks like, you can generate new motions that are likely to succeed, without needing to optimize a complicated reward or planning problem.

papers.title: Cosmos Policy: Fine-Tuning Video Models for Visuomotor Control and Planning
papers.contribution: Achieves 98.5% success on LIBERO and 67.1% on RoboCasa benchmarks, and highest average score on real-world bimanual manipulation tasks.

papers.title: Learning Part-Aware Dense 3D Feature Field For Generalizable Articulated Object Manipulation
papers.contribution: PA3FF consistently outperforms 2D and 3D baselines on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks with enhanced generalization.

papers.title: NavOL: Navigation Policy with Online Imitation Learning
papers.contribution: Collects over 2,000 trajectories per hour with domain randomization, demonstrating effectiveness on simulation benchmarks and real-world navigation tasks.

papers.title: SafeFlowMatcher: Safe and Fast Planning using Flow Matching with Control Barrier Functions
papers.contribution: The method achieves certified safety with finite-time convergence guarantees while producing faster, smoother paths than diffusion and flow matching baselines.

papers.title: ViPRA: Video Prediction for Robot Actions
papers.contribution: Achieves 16% gain on SIMBLER benchmark and 13% improvement on real-world manipulation tasks while enabling smooth continuous control up to 22 Hz and supporting generalization across embodiments.

papers.title: Adversarial Dual On-Policy Distillation from Expressive Teacher
papers.contribution: Beats strong baselines across six robot navigation, manipulation, and locomotion benchmarks with much stronger robustness under noisy or limited demonstrations.

papers.title: Block-wise Adaptive Caching for Accelerating Diffusion Policy
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 3x inference speedup for free as a training-free plugin without modifying parameters.

papers.title: Compose Your Policies! Improving Diffusion-based or Flow-based Robot Policies via Test-time Distribution-level Composition
papers.contribution: Composed policies exceed individual policy performance on Robomimic, PushT, and RoboTwin benchmarks with real-world validation.

papers.title: Compositional Visual Planning via Inference-Time Diffusion Scaling
papers.contribution: Training-free framework demonstrates significant improvements over baselines on 100 simulation tasks across 4 scenes, generalizing to unseen start-goal combinations.

papers.title: DADP: Domain Adaptive Diffusion Policy
papers.contribution: Superior zero-shot adaptation on locomotion and manipulation benchmarks with improved generalizability.

papers.title: Energy-based Compositional Diffusion Planning
papers.contribution: ECD achieves state-of-the-art success rates on OGBench tasks while maintaining inference speed comparable to heuristic stitching methods.

papers.title: FocalPolicy: Frequency-Optimized Chunking and Locally Anchored Flow Matching for Coherent Visuomotor Policy
papers.contribution: Outperforms existing approaches in learning coherent long-horizon actions with improved cross-chunk consistency.

papers.title: From Language to Locomotion: Retargeting-free Humanoid Control via Motion Latent Guidance
papers.contribution: Substantially reduces deployment latency, improves success rates and tracking accuracy, and produces smooth semantically aligned locomotion on real humanoids, extending to images, audio, and music.

papers.title: From Noise to Control: Parameterized Diffusion Policies
papers.contribution: Significantly improves adaptation on complex multimodal benchmarks in simulation and real-robot hardware compared to standard diffusion policy, especially for discovering novel behaviors.

papers.title: H$^3$DP: Triply‑Hierarchical Diffusion Policy for Visuomotor Learning
papers.contribution: H3DP achieves +27.5% average relative improvement over baselines on 44 simulation tasks and demonstrates superior performance on 4 challenging bimanual real-world manipulation tasks.

papers.title: HDFlow: Hierarchical Diffusion-Flow Planning for Long-horizon Tasks
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art on challenging furniture assembly tasks in simulation and real-world.

papers.title: Mixture of Horizons in Action Chunking
papers.contribution: Enables adaptive dynamic inference with 2.5× higher throughput; achieves consistent gains on both simulated and real-world robotic tasks.

papers.title: OMP: One-step Meanflow Policy with Directional Alignment
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on Adroit and Meta-World with superior success rate and trajectory accuracy while maintaining single-step efficiency.

papers.title: Plug-and-Play Label Map Diffusion for Universal Goal-Oriented Navigation
papers.contribution: PLMD effectively expands unknown map regions, integrates into existing navigation strategies, and achieves state-of-the-art on three GON tasks.

papers.title: Primary-Fine Decoupling for Action Generation in Robotic Imitation
papers.contribution: PF-DAG outperforms state-of-the-art across 56 tasks from Adroit, DexArt, and MetaWorld and generalizes to real-world tactile dexterous manipulation.

papers.title: SAD-Flower: Flow Matching for Safe, Admissible, and Dynamically Consistent Planning
papers.contribution: Outperforms generative baselines in ensuring constraint satisfaction across tasks, enabling test-time satisfaction of unseen constraints.

papers.title: STABLE: Simulation-Ready Tabletop Layout Generation via a Semantics–Physics Dual System
papers.contribution: Successfully generates simulation-ready tabletop scenes conforming to task instructions with significantly enhanced physical validity over prior art.

papers.title: Sparse ActionGen: Accelerating Diffusion Policy with Real-time Pruning
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 4× generation speedup on multiple robotic benchmarks without sacrificing performance.

papers.title: VITA: Vision-to-Action Flow Matching Policy
papers.contribution: Achieves 1.5x-2x faster inference while outperforming or matching SOTA on 9 simulation and 5 real-world robotic tasks.
